b: GM Hikaru Nakamura turned up at the Freestyle Friday on November 27 and won the event with a 10/11 score after saving himself from many tough situations, while GM Sina Movahed, IM Sergey Sklokin-Bagiyan, and FM Artin Ashraf all improved their chances to finish in the top eight of the combined tour standings, with impressive play and finishes.

There were a few dropouts during the tournament even before the finish line, the significant ones being GM Ian Nepomniachtchi withdrawing after eight rounds with four points and GM Jeffery Xiong after nine rounds with five points. Though Nepomniachtchi still maintains good chances to make it to the final cut, Xiong's chances have ended.

This leaves only one event of the series remaining to be played before the Freestyle Friday Championship (FFC), thus ending the hopes of anyone below the rank of 15 on the leaderboard. The next event, to be played on December 4, will be a tense affair.
IM Meri Arabidze once again topped the women's standings to gain the most points, while GM Alexandra Kosteniuk continues to lead the table.
Prizes: $400, $250, $150, and $100, plus $100 for Arabidze as top woman.

Though Nakamura is used to winning events regularly on this platform, the going was not smooth for him in the event, with many escapes from worse or even losing positions. However, his usual ability to defend positions stubbornly by effortlessly producing quality moves and superior clock handling stood him in good stead, and he escaped many losses.
The American player's most daring escape was against the runner-up of the tournament, GM Sina Movahed, in the seventh round.

However, Nakamura showed his fighting qualities the best when he required them the most. GM Jose Martinez took the lead with a clean 5/5 score when he played Nakamura, who was half a point behind, on the top board. The game was a true test of both the players' fighting qualities and had the inevitable drama of a blitz game.
GM Sam Sevian was another player who did not complete the tournament, but his game against GM Vladimir Fedoseev was one of the best fights of the entire event.
You can review the Freestyle Friday of November 27 on the Freestyle Chess YouTube channel. You can also review the games on our events page.

Freestyle Friday is Chess.com's weekly tournament dedicated to Freestyle Chess for titled players. The tournament begins at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time/17:00 Central European Time/21:30 Indian Standard Time.
